digest.component_or_area: source code comment hygiene & CI enforcement
propositions: Source code comments accumulate rot-prone references: commit SHAs (made unresolvable by rebase-on-submit), run/job/thread IDs (lost after retention expiry), and dated incident narratives that become stale; detector measured 15–17 violating sites at planning time, with census drifting ~1 new site per 17 commits.

Remediate all detector hits by moving historical narrative to the ticket system and citing ticket/epic/story/bug/ADR IDs in the form of grouped hex (4x4) or word-triple aliases, or by dropping rot-prone tokens and replacing with durable behavioral descriptions.

Implement a net-new CI guard (check_comment_hygiene.py) following the repo's check_*.py convention, wired into _build-and-test.yml, that blocks reintroduction of rot-prone refs: SHA-like hex ≥7 chars, run/job/thread IDs ≥8 digits, and dated-incident patterns (date + past-tense verb from enumerated set, excluding 'surfaced').

Guard acceptor must recognize ticket-ID citations (hex-grouped 4x4 or word-triple aliases) as sanctioned, reject false-accepts on path/extension context, and honor 'context: external' escape hatch for vendor-pinned refs.

Self-exclude the detector's own unit-test module (tests/unit/test_comment_hygiene_guard.py) via EXCLUDED_FILES tuple so live rot-prone fixture tokens do not trigger false failures, achieving zero in-tree suppressions.
Document policy in CONTRIBUTING.md that source code is authoritative for current state and concise rationale only; historical detail and incident context belong in the ticket system.
